nodes.speaker: Vera
nodes.text: The roof gave in a hundred years ago. The rain has been coming down ever since, and the tower has been letting it.

nodes.speaker: Vera
nodes.text: Whatever is keeping the light on up there does not know the sky fell.

nodes.speaker: Pell
nodes.text: I sell to anyone who comes down again. That is the whole business plan. Want to look?

nodes.speaker: Pell
nodes.text: Take your time. The rain is not going anywhere.

nodes.speaker: Pell
nodes.text: Then walk carefully. Things down here rust, and things up there do not.

nodes.speaker: Crystal Warden
nodes.text: You climbed here with a lantern.

nodes.speaker: Crystal Warden
nodes.text: Down where you come from, light is something you carry. Up here it is something we are.

nodes.speaker: Vera
nodes.text: The tower keeps humming. It did not need a guardian. It needed someone to notice.
The vault is quiet. The rain downstairs keeps falling anyway.

items.name: Heart of the Tower
items.description: It kept beating after the Warden stopped.

scenes.title: The rain got in first
scenes.synopsis: Vera enters the flooded gallery, meets the only merchant who still comes down, and learns the tower is inhabited.
scenes.prose:
The rain did not fall through the roof so much as live there. It had had a century to learn the shape of the room, and it had learned it well: the same three puddles, the same patient sound.

Pell had a landing, a crate and a business plan that fit in one sentence. Vera bought what she could carry and did not ask what he had seen come back down.

scenes.title: Something that is light
scenes.synopsis: At the top of the second floor the Warden explains the difference between carrying light and being it. Vera answers with a blade.
scenes.prose:
Up here the mist did not drift; it waited. The seams in the wall held a blue that had never been lit by anything.

The Warden spoke the way old things do, as if the sentence had been ready for a long time. Vera understood the argument and refused it anyway, and afterwards the tower kept humming, which she took to mean she had not put a light out. She had taken one.
